items.stem: Complete the statement: When shares are issued at a premium, the premium is credited to the …
options: share premium account
ordinary share capital account
general reserve
retained earnings
items.answer: share premium account
items.markingKey: Excess over nominal value → share premium (a capital reserve) [1].

items.stem: Explain why a company might make a bonus issue of shares even though it raises no cash.
items.answer: It brings issued share capital more in line with the capital employed, lowers the market price per share making shares more marketable, and signals confidence without paying a cash dividend.
items.markingKey: Two reasons [1 each] with explanation [1 each] [4]

items.stem: Explain why a rights issue is usually priced below the current market price.
items.answer: To encourage existing shareholders to take up the shares and ensure the issue is fully subscribed; it also compensates for dilution.
items.markingKey: Encourage take-up/full subscription [1]; compensates/attractive to shareholders [1] [2]

items.stem: Pinnacle Ltd has 840,000 ordinary shares of $0.50 each, share premium of $37,000 and retained earnings of $214,000. The directors make a 1 for 5 bonus issue, using the share premium account as far as possible. Calculate the balances on share capital, share premium and retained earnings after the issue.
items.answer: Share capital $504,000; share premium $0; retained earnings $167,000

options: capitalises reserves and raises no cash
raises cash from existing shareholders
reduces the number of shares in issue
increases total equity
items.answer: capitalises reserves and raises no cash
items.markingKey: Bonus issue: Dr reserves, Cr share capital; no cash received [1].

items.stem: Distinguish between a capital reserve and a revenue reserve, giving an example of each.
items.answer: A capital reserve (e.g. share premium, revaluation reserve) cannot be used to pay cash dividends; a revenue reserve (e.g. retained earnings, general reserve) arises from profits and can be distributed.
items.markingKey: Capital: not distributable + example [1]; revenue: distributable + example [1] [2]

items.stem: Explain what happens to the balance remaining on the forfeited shares account after forfeited shares are reissued.
items.answer: Any balance left after covering the discount on reissue is a capital profit and is transferred to the share premium account.
items.markingKey: Discount on reissue debited first [1]; remaining balance transferred to share premium [1] [2]

items.stem: Lynx Ltd offered 260,000 ordinary shares of $1 each at $2.00 per share, payable: application $0.50, allotment $1.30 (including the premium of $1.00) and a final call of $0.20. All money was received except the call on 20,000 shares, which were forfeited. These shares were later reissued as fully paid at $0.40 each. Calculate the amount credited to the forfeited shares account on forfeiture and the amount finally transferred to share premium.
items.answer: Forfeited shares $16,000; transfer to share premium $4,000
items.markingKey: Forfeiture: Dr share capital $20,000, Cr call $4,000, Cr forfeited shares $16,000 [2]; reissue: Dr bank $8,000, Dr forfeited shares $12,000, Cr share capital $20,000 [2]; balance $16,000 − $12,000 = $4,000 transferred to share premium [1]

items.stem: Complete the statement: The purpose of a capital redemption reserve is to …
options: increase the distributable profits
provide cash to pay dividends
maintain the company's capital so that creditors are protected when shares are redeemed out of profits
record the premium paid on redemption
items.answer: maintain the company's capital so that creditors are protected when shares are redeemed out of profits
items.markingKey: CRR replaces the share capital cancelled so the capital base is maintained [1].

items.stem: Explain why a company must transfer an amount to a capital redemption reserve when redeeming shares out of profits.
items.answer: Redemption reduces share capital; without a transfer, distributable reserves would be available to pay out as dividends and the capital that protects creditors would fall. The CRR locks up an equivalent amount.
items.markingKey: Share capital reduced [1]; creditors' buffer protected [1]; CRR non-distributable [1] [3]

items.stem: Give two reasons why a company might buy back its own ordinary shares.
items.answer: To return surplus cash to shareholders; to increase EPS/share price; to reduce the number of shareholders/prevent a takeover; to buy out a departing shareholder in a private company.
items.markingKey: Two reasons [1 each] with explanation [1 each] [4]

items.stem: Meridian Ltd redeems $290,000 of redeemable preference shares of $1 each at a premium of 10%. Before redemption it had retained earnings of $542,000 and share premium of $36,000. Calculate the transfer to the capital redemption reserve and the balance of retained earnings after the redemption.
items.answer: CRR $290,000; retained earnings $223,000
items.markingKey: CRR = nominal value redeemed $290,000 [1]; premium 10% × $290,000 = $29,000 charged to retained earnings [1]; retained earnings = $542,000 − $290,000 − $29,000 = $223,000 [1]

items.stem: Answer both parts. (a) Which shares can be redeemed by a company? (b) Complete the statement: When shares are redeemed entirely out of distributable profits, the amount transferred to the capital redemption reserve equals …

items.markingKey: (a) Only shares issued as redeemable may be redeemed; others may be bought back [1]. (b) CRR = nominal value redeemed − proceeds of any new issue [1].

items.stem: Explain the difference between redeeming shares and making a bonus issue in terms of their effect on cash and equity.
items.answer: Redemption pays cash out and reduces total equity; a bonus issue involves no cash and leaves total equity unchanged (it only reclassifies reserves as share capital).
items.markingKey: Redemption: cash out, equity falls [1]; bonus: no cash, equity unchanged [1] [2]

items.stem: Cobalt Ltd redeemed $90,000 of redeemable preference shares out of distributable profits. The accountant transferred $90,000 from the share premium account to the capital redemption reserve. Explain why this is incorrect and state the correct entry.
items.answer: The transfer must come from distributable profits (retained earnings), not from share premium, which is already a capital reserve. Correct entry: Dr retained earnings $90,000, Cr capital redemption reserve $90,000.
items.markingKey: Share premium is already non-distributable [1]; purpose is to lock up distributable profits [1]; Dr retained earnings, Cr CRR $90,000 [1] [3]

items.stem: Galaxy Ltd redeems $110,000 of redeemable preference shares of $1 each at par. Before redemption it had retained earnings of $440,000 and share premium of $25,000. What amount is transferred to the capital redemption reserve?

items.stem: Complete the statement: Debenture interest is …
options: an appropriation of profit like a dividend
credited to the share premium account
an expense (finance cost) that must be paid whether or not a profit is made
paid only if the directors declare it
items.answer: an expense (finance cost) that must be paid whether or not a profit is made
items.markingKey: Interest on debentures is a finance cost charged before tax [1].

items.stem: Explain two differences between debentures and ordinary shares from the point of view of the investor.
items.answer: Debenture holders are creditors, receive fixed interest whether or not profits are made and are repaid before shareholders; ordinary shareholders are owners, receive variable dividends, have votes and bear the most risk.
items.markingKey: Status creditor vs owner [1]; fixed interest vs variable dividend [1]; priority on winding up / votes [1]; risk [1] [4]

items.stem: Explain why a company might prefer to raise finance by issuing debentures rather than ordinary shares.
items.answer: Interest is tax deductible; no dilution of control; cost of debt usually lower; but increases gearing and fixed commitments.
items.markingKey: Two advantages [1 each] + development [1] [3]

items.stem: The draft financial statements of Pinnacle Ltd show debenture interest of $18,000 on $300,000 6% debentures deducted in the statement of changes in equity together with dividends. Explain why this is wrong and state the effect of correcting it on profit for the year.
items.answer: Debenture interest is a finance cost (expense), not an appropriation; it must be charged in the income statement. Profit for the year (before tax) falls by $18,000; retained earnings are unaffected overall.
items.markingKey: Interest is an expense owed to creditors [1]; show as finance cost in income statement [1]; profit reduced by $18,000 [1] [3]

During the following year: (1) a 1 for 5 rights issue was made at $1.20 and fully taken up; (2) all the preference shares were redeemed at par out of retained earnings; (3) $300,000 8% debentures were issued on the first day of the year. (a) Calculate the transfer to the capital redemption reserve and the closing retained earnings (before the profit for the year). (b) Calculate the debenture interest for the year and state where it appears in the financial statements.
items.answer: (a) CRR $50,000; retained earnings $687,000 (b) $24,000; finance costs in the income statement

items.stem: Answer both parts. (a) Complete the statement: The purpose of a capital redemption reserve is to … (b) Complete the statement: A capital redemption reserve can be used to …
items.answer: (a) maintain the company's capital so that creditors are protected when shares are redeemed out of profits (b) make a bonus issue of shares
items.markingKey: (a) CRR replaces the share capital cancelled so the capital base is maintained [1]. (b) CRR is a capital reserve; may be used for bonus issues only [1].

items.stem: Delta Ltd redeemed $60,000 of redeemable preference shares out of distributable profits. The accountant transferred $60,000 from the share premium account to the capital redemption reserve. Explain why this is incorrect and state the correct entry.
items.answer: The transfer must come from distributable profits (retained earnings), not from share premium, which is already a capital reserve. Correct entry: Dr retained earnings $60,000, Cr capital redemption reserve $60,000.
items.markingKey: Share premium is already non-distributable [1]; purpose is to lock up distributable profits [1]; Dr retained earnings, Cr CRR $60,000 [1] [3]

items.stem: Horizon plc redeems $260,000 of redeemable preference shares of $1 each at a premium of 5%. Before redemption it had retained earnings of $563,000 and share premium of $77,000. Calculate the transfer to the capital redemption reserve and the balance of retained earnings after the redemption.
items.answer: CRR $260,000; retained earnings $290,000
items.markingKey: CRR = nominal value redeemed $260,000 [1]; premium 5% × $260,000 = $13,000 charged to retained earnings [1]; retained earnings = $563,000 − $260,000 − $13,000 = $290,000 [1]

items.stem: Quetzal plc has 400,000 ordinary shares of $1 in issue, retained earnings of $455,000 and a bank balance of $234,000. It buys back and cancels 80,000 of its own shares at $1.80 each out of distributable profits. Calculate the balances on ordinary share capital, capital redemption reserve, retained earnings and bank after the purchase.
items.answer: Share capital $320,000; CRR $80,000; retained earnings $311,000; bank $90,000

items.stem: At 31 July 2025 the equity of Banyan Ltd was: ordinary shares of $1 $400,000, $180,000 redeemable preference shares of $1, share premium $179,000, retained earnings $316,000. During the following year: (1) a 1 for 4 rights issue was made at $1.80 and fully taken up; (2) all the preference shares were redeemed at a 10% premium out of retained earnings; (3) $150,000 5% debentures were issued on the first day of the year. (a) Calculate the cash raised by the rights issue and the new share premium balance. (b) Calculate the debenture interest for the year and state where it appears in the financial statements.
items.answer: (a) $180,000; share premium $259,000 (b) $7,500; finance costs in the income statement

items.stem: The draft financial statements of Meridian Ltd show debenture interest of $20,000 on $250,000 8% debentures deducted in the statement of changes in equity together with dividends. Explain why this is wrong and state the effect of correcting it on profit for the year.
items.answer: Debenture interest is a finance cost (expense), not an appropriation; it must be charged in the income statement. Profit for the year (before tax) falls by $20,000; retained earnings are unaffected overall.
items.markingKey: Interest is an expense owed to creditors [1]; show as finance cost in income statement [1]; profit reduced by $20,000 [1] [3]

items.stem: Delta Ltd issued $300,000 5% debentures 3 months before its year end on 31 March 2026. Calculate the debenture interest to be charged in the income statement.

Meridian Ltd needs funds for a new factory in Peru. It issues $350,000 7% debentures 9 months before its year end. Profit from operations is $205,000 and equity is $790,000. (a) Calculate the debenture interest charge for the current year and for a full year. (b) State the journal entry to record the accrued interest at the year end if none has been paid.
items.answer: (a) $18,375; full year $24,500 (b) Dr finance costs (debenture interest) $18,375; Cr accrued expenses (interest payable) $18,375
